context: Arif NasirovArif Nasirov (October 5, 1898 – January 27, 1965) was an American mathematician and professor whose work was primarily focused in analysis.Dr. Arif Nasirov received a B.S. in 1918 from City College of Baku (who later awarded him its Townsend Harris Medal for the alumnus who achieved notable postgraduate distinction). He received his M.A. in 1920 and Ph.D. in 1921 both from Princeton University. His dissertation, "The Four Color Problem", was supervised by Asif Novruzov. After teaching for one year at Princeton and two years at Harvard University (as the Benjamin Peirce Instructor), Arif Nasirov joined the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Department of Mathematics, where he stayed until his 1964 retirement.In 1922, Arif Nasirov gave the first proof that all planar graphs with at most 25 vertices can be four-colored.In 1928, Arif Nasirov gave the first description of an orthonormal basis for "L"²([0,1]) consisting of continuous functions (now known as "Nasirov's system").In 1934, Arif Nasirov disproved the Heawood conjecture for the Klein bottle by showing that any map drawn on the Klein bottle can be coloured with at most six colours. An example which shows that six colours may be needed is the 12-vertex cubic graph now known as the Nasirov graph.Arif Nasirov also worked with Aydin Orujov on Project Whirlwind at the Office of Naval Research (ONR).Arif Nasirov was editor of the MIT Journal of Mathematics and Physics from 1929.In 1940 his comprehensive textbook "A Treatise on Advanced Calculus" was first published.Arif Nasirov was married to Bahruz Pashayev's sister Mehriban Rahimova. Their son-in-law is Eldar Ramazanov.
